name: Takarkori early dairying
description: Food residues and animal remains at Takarkori rock shelter support a pastoral system that included processing milk products.

impact.note: Milk processing gave Saharan herders a new food source, carried on by later African pastoralists, with reach kept regional on present evidence.

date.label: Middle Pastoral contexts approximately 5210–3660 BCE
date.basis: The 2018 review reports the Middle Pastoral Takarkori range as 5210–3660 BCE in Table 1; pottery lipid interpretations are context-associated.

events.statement: Food residues and animal remains at Takarkori rock shelter support a pastoral system that included processing milk products.

evidence.supports: The review gives Middle Pastoral context 5210–3660 BCE and discusses dairy residues and cattle remains.
Original compound-specific carbon isotope measurements distinguish ruminant dairy fat in selected Middle Pastoral potsherds.

events.caveats: Lipid residues identify ruminant dairy and are dated by the pottery context. The species that provided milk and how it was processed remain open.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest supported event for this scoped case, not a universal priority claim. Residues do not identify the animal species for every vessel, amounts consumed, or the first emergence of dairying.

caveats: Residues do not identify the animal species for every vessel, amounts consumed, or the first emergence of dairying.

research.note: Independent review of marked source facets on 2026-11-09; archaeological and historical interpretations retain the stated limitations.

unresolved.note: Early Pastoral caprine remains precede the dairy-bearing ceramics. Identify milk species and trace herd and settlement continuity through the Early and Middle Pastoral assemblages.

evidence.locator: Abstract and caprine distribution map, panel b, site 30
evidence.supports: Direct caprine bone dating precedes the Middle Pastoral dairy evidence at Takarkori.
